history.request: Build a breakfast shop ordering system with three tabs. Tab 1 "Order": customers pick items (egg crepe $3.50, radish cake $4.00, teppan noodles $5.50, chicken nuggets $4.50, milk tea $3.00, soy milk $2.50), change quantities, enter a table number and send the order. Tab 2 "Kitchen": orders listed by time; each order moves from "To do" to "Cooking" to "Done", each state in its own color. Tab 3 "Sales": today's number of orders and total sales.
history.summary: A breakfast shop ordering system with three tabs. The Order tab lets customers choose menu items, adjust quantities, enter a table number and send the order. The Kitchen tab lists orders by time and lets staff move each one from To do to Cooking to Done, with a distinct color for each state. The Sales tab shows today's order count and total sales. The static web front end talks to a Python standard-library JSON API that keeps all data in memory.

history.request: (m-vvk9f) When ordering, customers should choose "Dine in" or "Take out", and the kitchen board should show it.; (laoban-cli-test) [breakfast-en-web] The kitchen should be able to mark an item as sold out; sold-out items turn grey on the order page and cannot be picked.; (laoban-cli-test2) [breakfast-en-api] Add today's top three items to the Sales tab.
history.summary: A breakfast shop ordering system with three tabs. On the Order tab, customers choose menu items, adjust quantities, enter a table number, pick Dine in or Take out, and send the order. Sold-out items appear grey and cannot be picked. The Kitchen tab lists orders by time with a Dine in / Take out label. Staff can move each order from To do to Cooking to Done, and can mark menu items as sold out or available again. The Sales tab shows today's order count, total sales and the top three items sold. The static web front end talks to a Python standard-library JSON API that keeps all data in memory.

endpoints.purpose: Return the fixed list of menu items with id, name, price and soldOut flag.
Mark a menu item as sold out or available again by setting soldOut to true or false.
Create an order from a table number, an order type (dine_in or take_out) and item quantities. Sold-out items are rejected; the server computes the total and sets status to todo.
List orders (including their order type) sorted by creation time, optionally filtered by status.
Advance an order from todo to cooking to done.
Return today's number of orders, total sales and the top three items by quantity sold.

modules.name: server.py
modules.purpose: Single standard-library Python module (http.server) with the menu and its sold-out flags, in-memory order store, validation including order type and sold-out checks, status transitions, sales and top-item calculation, and JSON routing.

modules.name: index.html
modules.purpose: Page structure with the three tabs (Order, Kitchen, Sales) and their panels, including the Dine in / Take out selector on the Order tab and the menu availability section on the Kitchen tab.

modules.name: app.js
modules.purpose: Tab switching, API calls, order form logic with order type and sold-out handling, kitchen board rendering with order type labels and sold-out toggles, and sales display including the top three items.

modules.name: style.css
modules.purpose: Layout, tab styling, menu cards, distinct colors for To do, Cooking and Done, grey sold-out menu cards, order type badges and the top-items list.

plan.notes: #1「customers should choose Dine in or Take out」and its supporting vote are implemented as an order type field shown on the kitchen board. The reply to #1「Could take-out orders go first?」was not followed: it would change the kitchen ordering rule, which nobody else asked for, and could leave dine-in orders waiting indefinitely. Orders stay sorted by creation time, and the clear Dine in / Take out label lets staff prioritise by hand. #2「sold out items turn grey」is implemented with a new endpoint and toggles in the Kitchen tab, since the kitchen needs a place to mark items. #3「today's top three items」is added to the existing GET /sales/today response rather than a new endpoint, to keep the change small.
steps: In the API module, add an order type field (dine_in or take_out) to the order record. POST /orders requires it and rejects any other value with a clear message.
In the API module, add a sold-out flag to each menu item, false by default. GET /menu returns it, and POST /orders rejects orders containing a sold-out item.
Add PATCH /menu/{id}/sold-out, which takes a boolean soldOut, updates the item under the existing lock and returns the updated item. Unknown item ids return 404.

Extend GET /sales/today with a topItems list of up to three items (id, name, quantity sold), ranked by total quantity across today's orders. Ties are broken by menu order and the list is empty when there are no orders.
In index.html, add a Dine in / Take out selector to the Order tab and a menu availability section to the Kitchen tab.

In app.js, require an order type on the Order tab before submitting and send it with the order. Render sold-out menu items with a grey style and disabled plus and minus controls, and refresh the menu when the Order tab opens.
In app.js, show a Dine in / Take out label on each kitchen order card. Add sold-out toggle buttons for each menu item in the Kitchen tab, calling PATCH /menu/{id}/sold-out.
In app.js, show the top three items (name and quantity) in the Sales tab, with an empty-state message when there are no sales.
In style.css, add the grey sold-out menu card style, distinct badges for Dine in and Take out, and the styling for the sold-out toggles and top-items list, keeping the responsive layout.

Test the flow: place dine-in and take-out orders and check the labels in Kitchen. Mark an item sold out and confirm it is grey and unselectable on the Order tab and that the API rejects it. Mark it available again, and check that the top three items in Sales match the orders.
